       DEFENDANT META PLATFORMS, INC.’S RESPONSE IN OPPOSITION TO
      PLAINTIFF’S MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE SUPPLEMENTAL COMPLAINT

          Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc., (“Meta”) by and through its undersigned counsel, hereby

  respectfully opposes Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine’s Motion for Leave to File a Supplemental

  Complaint pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(d), Dkt. No. 26. Meta hereby joins,

  adopts and incorporates all applicable arguments and requested relief contained in Defendant

  National Center for Missing & Exploited Children’s (“NCMEC”) Opposition to Plaintiff’s Motion

  for Leave to File a Supplemental Complaint (Dkt. No. 28). In further support, Meta states as

  follows:

     I.      Procedural History

          As described in Meta’s Motion to Dismiss the First Amended Complaint (“FAC”), Plaintiff

  has filed a series of actions against Meta across several different courts, all stemming from the

  alleged disablement of his Facebook account. See Dkt. No. 22 at 3-5. Across all of these actions,

  Plaintiff has routinely filed amended complaints (or sought leave to do so), consistently delaying



                                                  1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD            Document 53        Filed 09/03/26     Page 2 of 5 PageID# 456




  decision on motions to dismiss across those actions. Indeed, since September 9, 2025 (when

  Plaintiff filed his first complaint against Meta in the United States District Court for the Northern

  District of California), Plaintiff has filed 12 distinct complaints against Meta across four distinct

  courts (not counting his proposed supplemental complaints in the instant action).

           Plaintiff’s present request for leave to supplement continues his strategy of seeking

  repeated amendment to delay decision on motions to dismiss. Indeed, in this court alone, Plaintiff

  has:

              •    Filed a complaint based on the allegations raised in the FAC against NCMEC and
                   Defendant Katie Hall (together, the “NCMEC Defendants) in a distinct action
                   (Ballentine v. Nat’l Ctr. for Missing & Exploited Children, No. 1:26-cv-1341 (E.D.
                   Va.);
              •    Filed a motion for leave to amend that complaint to add claims against Meta;
              •    Voluntarily dismissed that action after the NCMEC Defendants opposed his request
                   for leave to amend;
              •    Filed the complaint and FAC against the NCMEC Defendants and Meta in the
                   instant action; and
              •    Following motions to dismiss, filed the present motion for leave to supplement, and
                   has indicated a future intention to file a second such motion.

  See Dkt. No. 22 at 5.

     II.      Plaintiff’s Supplemental Allegations are Futile.

           “[T]he standards used by a district court in ruling on a motion to amend or on a motion to

  supplement [a complaint] are nearly identical.” Franks v. Ross, 313 F.3d 184, 198, n. 15 (4th Cir.

  2002). In either case, “leave to amend a pleading should be denied. . . when the amendment would

  be futile.” Brannen v. Selene Finance, LP, No. 2:18-cv-602, 2019 WL 13251099, at *2, 5 (E.D.

  Va. Nov. 14, 2019) (denying leave to file supplemental complaint where “it would be futile to

  permit” Plaintiff’s “supplemental pleading” where his “right to relief” remained “a matter of pure

  speculation”).




                                                    2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD                 Document 53           Filed 09/03/26          Page 3 of 5 PageID# 457




           As to Plaintiff’s supplemental allegations regarding the NCMEC Defendants, Meta fully

  adopts the arguments in NCMEC’s Opposition, which explain why the supplemental allegations

  are “frivolous and futile,” unnecessary, and “a further attempt to prolong” the litigation. Dkt. No.

  32 at 4-5.

           As to Plaintiff’s supplemental allegations regarding Meta, Plaintiff’s proposed supplement

  alleges only that in a motion to dismiss in a separate action brought by Plaintiff (Ballentine v. Meta

  Platforms, Inc., No. 3:26-cv-05939-RFL (N.D. Cal.)), Meta described Plaintiff’s litigation against

  the NCMEC as one of several actions Plaintiff has brought arising from the alleged disablement

  of his Facebook account. See Dkt. No. 26-2 at ¶ 22-24. Plaintiff asserts that Meta’s “citation of the

  present action . . . demonstrates that, by August 13, 2026, Meta had actual knowledge of the

  existence of the present action” and “of the relationship between the present action and the

  Northern District of California proceeding.” Id. ¶¶ 25, 32.

           But Meta’s knowledge, as of August 13, 2026, that Plaintiff sued NCMEC has no relevance

  whatsoever to Plaintiff’s claims against Meta, which are both premised on Plaintiff’s assertion that

  Meta somehow conspired with NCMEC in connection with letters that NCMEC sent to Plaintiff

  on April 22, 2026. Because Plaintiff’s supplemental allegations against Meta are plainly irrelevant

  to his claims or the issues raised in Meta’s motion to dismiss, amendment would be futile and

  Plaintiff’s motion should be denied. See Dacha v. Moody, No. 3:24-cv-713, 2026 WL 625494, at

  *15 (E.D. Va. Mar. 5, 2026) (denying motion to supplement under Rule 15(d) because

  “[p]ermitting [plaintiff] to supplement the records with the facts” identified in the motion to

  supplement “would be futile” where the facts could not plausibly serve “as a factual basis for any

  claim” against defendants).1

             For the foregoing reasons, Meta respectfully requests that the Court deny Plaintiff’s Motion

  for Leave to File a Supplemental Complaint.
